sources.title: Microsoft Job Objects
sources.locator: Creating/Managing Processes; Limits; Managing Job Objects; Process Tree
sources.governing_observation: Membership determines accounting and termination; CreateProcess inheritance has WMI/breakaway exceptions; nesting starts with Windows 8; kill-on-close depends on the last handle.
sources.assessment_scope: Worker ownership, descendant capture, shutdown and scope of cancellation.
sources.limits: No target-host capability or security sandbox established.

sources.title: Basic Job Object limits
sources.governing_observation: Job memory restricts the sum of committed memory; commits exceeding the limit fail. Notification-only limits differ.

sources.title: Extended Job Object limits
sources.governing_observation: The limits concern committed virtual memory and require corresponding flags. Job and process caps are independent.
sources.assessment_scope: Meaning of Windows cap, measurement and override conditions.
sources.limits: Commit limits are not a physical RAM/RSS ceiling.

sources.title: AssignProcessToJobObject
sources.governing_observation: Assignment requires handle rights, session compatibility and valid nesting; earlier memory operations are not examined.
sources.assessment_scope: Inert/suspended launch, assignment failure and supported-version caveats.

sources.title: Linux cgroup v2
sources.governing_observation: Forked children inherit the current cgroup; later migration leaves existing descendants behind. Memory accounting has qualifications; high and max are different controls.
sources.assessment_scope: Launch containment, capability fallback and accounting.
sources.limits: Installed kernel, delegation, HugeTLB configuration and actual workload remain unknown.

sources.title: systemd cgroup delegation
sources.version_context: Live guidance; controller-list request since v236; hierarchy changes v256/v258
sources.governing_observation: Delegate requests a subtree/controllers; availability and enablement differ. Inner-node placement and single-owner rules constrain setup.
sources.assessment_scope: Conditional rootless adapters and optional managed-unit approach.

sources.title: SQLite WAL
sources.version_context: Live official documentation; section 11 includes 2026-08-24 update
sources.governing_observation: WAL is same-host, single-writer and reader-sensitive for checkpoint completion. The reset race is fixed in 3.51.3 and listed backports, under specific multi-connection write/checkpoint timing.
sources.limits: No claim that the target bundles SQLite or that DB transactions commit report files.

sources.title: SQLite release history
sources.governing_observation: The current upstream release and WAL-reset fix entries support the final release statements and correction of older top-release metadata.

sources.title: SQLite synchronous
sources.locator: FULL/NORMAL WAL behavior, lines 820-844 in retrieved text
sources.governing_observation: NORMAL in WAL can lose recent commits after system/power failure; application-crash durability differs. FULL adds a per-commit sync.

sources.title: SQLite transactions
sources.governing_observation: IMMEDIATE takes the write transaction at start and can encounter SQLITE_BUSY; transactions and error handling remain local to the database.

sources.title: SQLite result codes
sources.governing_observation: Concurrent writers can produce BUSY; busy handlers and transaction mode are relevant.

sources.title: SQLite transactional guarantee
sources.governing_observation: The guarantee concerns a database transaction; configuration/storage conditions still matter.
sources.limits: Upstream testing is not execution by the candidate or evaluator.

sources.title: SQLite recent news
sources.governing_observation: The date-bounded upstream version agrees with the proposal.

sources.title: VS Code API
sources.governing_observation: Promise settlement governs progress lifetime. Notification progress supports discrete progress and cancellation UI; the token is cooperative.

sources.title: VS Code extension host
sources.governing_observation: Hosts differ by runtime/location; this does not supply a per-task boundary.
sources.limits: Evaluator could open the page; predecessors disclosed their direct-open failures.

sources.title: VS Code extension-host progress bridge
sources.version_context: Moving main; independent API lookup observed 80101bda7057c6f2081cc64f510b6fa3cbf2de5b
sources.governing_observation: Cancellable operations get a token source; cancel signals it, while the callback promise governs completion.
sources.limits: The evaluator lookup does not retroactively pin predecessor retrievals. Copyright Microsoft; MIT license.

sources.title: VS Code main-thread progress bridge
sources.version_context: Moving main; same independently observed commit context
sources.governing_observation: The UI cancellation callback invokes the extension-host bridge; ending progress resolves its tracking promise.
sources.assessment_scope: Cooperative signal, not forced process termination.
sources.limits: Read, not executed; copyright Microsoft, MIT license.

sources.title: VS Code issue 93822
sources.locator: Manual Testing; API declaration pinned to 21293c4; status
sources.governing_observation: The issue is an upstream manual progress test plan, with a notification-cancel caveat; closure is not a target-app or candidate validation pass.

sources.title: Shreedhar/Varghese DRR paper
sources.locator: Indexed primary-paper text: section III p377 and conclusion p385
sources.governing_observation: Deficit carries unused quantum across rounds; fairness is normalized transmitted service among backlogged flows. The paper discusses whole-unit applications beyond packets.
sources.assessment_scope: Qualified qualitative analogy to variable jobs, not imported job/memory/latency guarantees.
sources.limits: PDF is image-only; local text extraction unavailable and screenshot transport returned only a locator. Independent inspection used indexed text of the primary paper. All proofs and simulations were not audited.

evidence_policy: Compact original observations and exact public links only. Body digests describe retrieved public source bytes; raw source corpora are not retained. No code was executed.
